title: Pocklington Lancaster Memorial
crew_summary: 5 killed (2 survived injured); 2 civilians also killed; pilot Plt Off. Joseph Watson Thompson, DFM
memorial_type: Memorial bench and crash site marker
narrative: On the evening of 29 March 1943, the crew of Halifax JB848 were detailed for a major operation against Berlin. The aircraft began its takeoff run from Pocklington airfield but during the climb-out the pilot lost control. The Halifax stalled, turned onto its back and crashed in a catastrophic explosion near Thirsk's Mill and Pocklington School at West Green, just outside the airfield boundary. All crew were killed instantly in the resulting fireball. The crash site remained undisturbed for over 70 years until 2014, when excavation work for a new doctors' surgery uncovered a Rolls-Royce Merlin engine and various aircraft parts. The discovery prompted local residents to recover, clean and restore the engine, which was subsequently installed as a memorial to the crew.
cause_of_loss: Pilot lost control on takeoff; aircraft stalled, inverted and crashed
memorial_details:
Name: Avro Lancaster ED393
Type: Stone of remembrance
Description: Large piece of rough-cut limestone with one finished, diagonal face, into which a circular, black, slate tablet is inset. The dedication is depicted in raised, white capital letters.
Inscription: ON 27TH NOVEMBER 1943 AT 02:15/ LANCASTER BOMBER ED393 VN-K/CRASHED NEAR THIS SPOT./ AIRBORNE FROM SKELLINGTHORPE FOR BERLIN AT 17:08/ BUT DIVERTED ON ITS RETURN DUE TO FOG,/ FIRST TO MELBOURNE AND THEN POCKLINGTON/ BEFORE RUNNING OUT OF FUEL, STRIKING TREES, A FARMHOUSE/ AND CRASHING INTO INGS HOUSE./ (names)/ DEDICATED TO THEIR MEMORY BY/ HH 'CHARLIE' ROSS/ WITNESS AND SON OF ONE OF THE RESCUERS
Location: Canal Head picnic area Off York Road (A1079 Pocklington East Yorkshire Antrim YO42 1NW England
Grid Ref: SE 79980 47340
Coordinates: 53.916043339688,-0.783782294012
Photos: https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/127/279/large_ey_canal_head_2.jpg; https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/127/280/large_ey_canal_head_3.jpg; https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/127/281/large_ey_canal_head_1.jpg

external_narratives.summary: IWM War Memorials Register entry for the crew of Lancaster Bomber ED393 memorial at Pocklington. Records the stone of remembrance dedicated by HH 'Charlie' Ross, a witness to the crash.
key_details: Dedicated by crash witness HH 'Charlie' Ross

external_narratives.summary: Detailed account of Lancaster ED393 VN-K of 50 Squadron. The aircraft diverted from fog-bound Lincolnshire to Yorkshire on return from Berlin, lost height in landing circuit and crashed at Canal Head, Pocklington, destroying the Canal Head public house and cottages on Ramsdale Terrace.
key_details: Diverted due to fog over Lincolnshire
Crashed at Canal Head destroying public house and cottages

external_narratives.summary: Squadron association memorial page for ED393 VN-K at Pocklington. Provides detailed context from the squadron's perspective, including the Berlin operation that night and the diversion circumstances.
key_details: Listed on squadron association memorial page
Part of 50 Squadron's Berlin operations November 1943

external_narratives.summary: Local history group research into wartime aircraft crashes around Pocklington, including the ED393 crash at Canal Head. Provides community perspective on the impact of multiple crashes on the town during the war.
key_details: Local history group maintains detailed crash records
Multiple wartime crashes documented around Pocklington

remembrance.service_description: The crew of this aircraft are remembered at the annual No. 50 & No. 61 Squadrons Association memorial service at Skellingthorpe, near their wartime base. The 2026 service takes place on 7 June — Birchwood memorial at 11:30, village memorial at 14:00.

events.name: 2026 Memorial Service at Skellingthorpe
events.description: Annual service at Birchwood memorial (11:30) and village memorial (14:00). AGM Saturday 6 June at 17:00.
